selected.hook_line: If food is everywhere, how can eating the same few things still fail you?
selected.viewer_expectation: Plenty of food plus fresh water should cover the basic needs for long-term survival.
selected.visible_contradiction: The camp has lots to eat, but nearly every meal comes from the same two foods.
selected.frame_zero: A full water barrel, coconuts and racks of fish fill the frame, while the meal plate holds only fish and coconut.
selected.character_action: The captain compares the packed food rack with the narrow meal, gives a small skeptical look, then studies the available island foods through the spyglass.
selected.reaction: A raised eyebrow and brief pause show that plenty of food is not the same as a complete diet.
selected.activity: testing whether abundance also means enough variety
selected.location: a simple island food shelter beside coconut trees
selected.topic_link: A person can have enough calories yet still miss nutrients the body needs if the diet stays too limited.
selected.factual_anchor: Food and water are important, but having supplies does not remove every long-term survival problem.
selected.payoff: Living for many years would require a diet that keeps supplying the nutrients the body needs, not just a large amount of food.

entry_bridge.a_end: The captain holds the spyglass toward the repeated foods, with the narrow eyepiece at his visible eye and the wide objective facing them.
entry_bridge.b_start: From an oblique rear-side view, the same correct spyglass orientation points toward the food before the view matches forward.
entry_bridge.reveal: The repeated meals become a closer look at what the diet provides and what a very narrow diet can miss.
entry_bridge.world_entry: A host-free close view compares several repeated island meals with the range of nutrients a human body needs over time.

novelty.prop_family: fish rack, coconuts and meal plate
novelty.reveal_family: repeated meals expose a long-term nutrition gap
